target: C'est un problème dont la solution n'est pas simple.
english: It's a problem whose solution is not simple.
tip: 'Ce dont' = what...about/of: 'ce dont j'ai besoin' = what I need (avoir besoin de).

target: Le bus qui s'arrête devant notre immeuble va au centre-ville.
english: The bus that stops in front of our building goes downtown.
tip: "Qui" never changes form regardless of the gender or number of the antecedent.

target: Si elle avait pris le bus, elle ne serait pas arrivée en retard.
english: If she had taken the bus, she wouldn't have arrived late.
tip: "Serait arrivée" uses être in conditionnel passé because arriver uses être as auxiliary.

target: Il aurait fallu réserver à l'avance.
english: We should have booked in advance.
tip: "Il aurait fallu" = conditionnel passé of falloir. Expresses something that should have been done.

target: Quand tu auras fini tes devoirs, appelle-moi.
english: When you finish your homework, call me.
tip: Futur antérieur: auras (future of avoir) + past participle. Expresses a future action completed before another.

target: La chanson que tu chantes est très belle.
english: The song you're singing is very beautiful.
tip: 'Que' for direct objects: 'la chanson que tu chantes'. The thing being sung is the direct object.

target: J'avais oublié de fermer la porte en partant.
english: I had forgotten to close the door when leaving.
tip: Plus-que-parfait of oublier: avais oublié. Used for a past action prior to another past event.

target: Quand elle aura accouché, nous irons la voir à l'hôpital.
english: When she's had the baby, we'll go see her at the hospital.
tip: Futur antérieur can express conjecture about the past: 'il aura oublié' = he must have forgotten.

target: C'est la ville où je suis né.
english: It's the city where I was born.
tip: "Où" replaces a place or time complement in the relative clause.

target: La décision que tu as prise est courageuse.
english: The decision you made is courageous.
tip: "Prise" agrees with "la décision" (feminine singular): pris → prise.

target: C'est un film dont j'ai oublié le titre.
english: It's a movie whose title I've forgotten.
tip: "Dont" replaces possessive "de": le titre du film → dont j'ai oublié le titre.

target: Le père voulait que son fils devînt avocat.
english: The father wanted his son to become a lawyer.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of devenir: devînt, from passé simple stem devin-.

target: La plage où nous allons chaque été est calme.
english: The beach where we go every summer is calm.
tip: "Où" replaces place expressions: nous allons à la plage → la plage où nous allons.

target: L'entreprise dont il est le directeur est en pleine croissance.
english: The company he is the director of is growing rapidly.
tip: "Dont" replaces "de" in all constructions: être directeur de → dont.

target: Je craignais qu'elle ne mourût de froid.
english: I feared she might die of cold.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of mourir: mourût. Note the expletive 'ne' after craindre.

target: Il avait plu toute la nuit et les rues étaient inondées.
english: It had rained all night and the streets were flooded.
tip: Plus-que-parfait sets up cause: 'il avait plu toute la nuit' → result: 'les rues étaient inondées'.

target: Nous voulions qu'ils fissent le travail.
english: We wanted them to do the work.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of faire: fissent, from passé simple stem fi-.

target: J'aurais préféré rester à la maison ce soir.
english: I would have preferred to stay home tonight.
tip: Conditionnel passé for regret: 'j'aurais préféré' = I would have preferred. Common for wishful thinking.

target: Si elle avait su, elle ne serait jamais venue.
english: If she had known, she would never have come.
tip: 'Si elle avait su' – plus-que-parfait in the si-clause. The 'if only she had known' construction.

target: Si tu m'avais écouté, tu n'aurais pas fait cette erreur.
english: If you had listened to me, you wouldn't have made this mistake.
tip: Plus-que-parfait: auxiliary (avoir/être) in imparfait + past participle. The 'past of the past'.

target: Elle avait rencontré son mari à l'université il y a vingt ans.
english: She had met her husband at university twenty years ago.
tip: Plus-que-parfait of rencontrer: avait rencontré. Used for a past event before another past reference.

target: Il fallait qu'il comprît la situation.
english: He had to understand the situation.
tip: The imperfect subjunctive of comprendre: comprît, from passé simple stem compri-.

target: Or, personne n'avait prévu cette situation.
english: Now, no one had foreseen this situation.
tip: Or: 'now/however', introduces a new and often contradictory fact.

target: Il fallait que chacun fît sa part.
english: Everyone had to do their part.
tip: In modern French, the imperfect subjunctive is replaced by the present subjunctive in all but the most formal writing.

target: J'avais espéré te revoir avant ton départ.
english: I had hoped to see you again before your departure.
tip: Plus-que-parfait can express an unfulfilled past hope: avais espéré = had hoped.

target: Elle avait toujours rêvé de visiter le Japon.
english: She had always dreamed of visiting Japan.
tip: Plus-que-parfait describes a past state prior to a narrative: avait rêvé = had dreamed.

target: Il désirait que nous eussions le courage de parler.
english: He wished we had the courage to speak.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of avoir: eussions, from passé simple stem eu-.

target: Il aurait été préférable de demander l'avis d'un expert.
english: It would have been preferable to ask an expert's opinion.
tip: "Il aurait été" = conditionnel passé impersonnel of être.

target: Dès que le colis sera arrivé, je vous enverrai un courriel.
english: As soon as the package has arrived, I'll send you an email.
tip: Futur antérieur with être: sera arrivé. Arriver takes être.

target: On regrettait qu'il ne fût plus parmi nous.
english: They regretted he was no longer among us.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of être: fût. Standard literary form.

target: Il était temps qu'il se tût.
english: It was time for him to be quiet.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of se taire: se tût, from passé simple stem tu-.

target: Il semblait qu'il eût oublié sa promesse.
english: It seemed he had forgotten his promise.
tip: Pluperfect subjunctive: eût oublié. Literary equivalent of 'ait oublié'.

target: Quand bien même il aurait raison, je refuserais.
english: Even if he were right, I would refuse.
tip: Quand bien même + conditionnel: emphatic hypothetical concession.

target: Pour peu qu'on lui demande, il est prêt à aider.
english: If you so much as ask him, he's ready to help.
tip: Mixed conditionals possible: 'si j'avais étudié (past), je serais médecin (present result)'.

target: Si j'avais eu le choix, j'aurais voyagé en première classe.
english: If I had had the choice, I would have travelled first class.
tip: Double compound past: 'si j'avais eu le choix, j'aurais voyagé'. Both auxiliaries in the si-clause and result.

target: Il est conseillé de boire beaucoup d'eau.
english: It is advisable to drink plenty of water.
tip: 'Il est conseillé de' = it is advisable to. Another impersonal construction for recommendations.

target: Elle désirait que nous partissions avant la nuit.
english: She wished us to leave before nightfall.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of partir: partissions, from passé simple stem parti-.

target: Il est peu probable que nous ayons des nouvelles aujourd'hui.
english: It is unlikely we will have news today.
tip: 'Se' + verb can express passive meaning: 'le français se parle au Québec' = French is spoken in Quebec.

target: Même si tu me suppliais, je ne changerais pas d'avis.
english: Even if you begged me, I wouldn't change my mind.
tip: Même si + imparfait, conditionnel: emphatic unreal condition.

target: Il importait qu'elle suivît les instructions.
english: It mattered that she follow the instructions.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of suivre: suivît, from passé simple stem suivi-.

target: Bien que nous fussions fatigués, nous poursuivîmes.
english: Although we were tired, we continued.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of être: fussions. First person plural.

target: Elle a voulu savoir où j'habitais.
english: She wanted to know where I lived.
tip: Indirect question keeps declarative word order: 'où j'habitais' (not *'où habitais-je').

target: Il est recommandé de réserver à l'avance.
english: It is recommended to book in advance.
tip: 'Il est recommandé de' – impersonal passive. The subject 'il' is a formal placeholder.

target: Si j'étais toi, je n'accepterais pas cette offre.
english: If I were you, I wouldn't accept that offer.
tip: 'Si j'étais toi' – imparfait after 'si' for present hypotheticals. Never conditional after 'si'.

target: Sans cette erreur, il aurait obtenu le poste.
english: Without that mistake, he would have gotten the job.
tip: Sans + noun can replace a si clause in past unreal conditions.

target: Le professeur a fait travailler les élèves toute la matinée.
english: The teacher made the students work all morning.
tip: Faire + infinitive: 'to make someone do something'.

target: En supposant qu'il accepte, quand commencerait-il ?
english: Supposing he accepts, when would he start?
tip: Si + présent → futur: 'si tu viens, je serai content'. Real/likely condition.

target: Si on m'avait prévenu, j'aurais agi autrement.
english: If I had been warned, I would have acted differently.
tip: Mixed past condition: 'si on m'avait prévenu, j'aurais agi' – both clauses refer to unreal past.

target: Pour peu qu'il fasse un effort, il réussira.
english: If he makes even the slightest effort, he'll succeed.
tip: 'Pour peu que' + subjunctive: 'for little that' = if only slightly. Triggers subjunctive.

target: Dans la mesure où c'est possible, nous vous aiderons.
english: Insofar as it is possible, we will help you.
tip: Dans la mesure où: 'insofar as/to the extent that'.

target: À supposer que le projet échoue, quelles seraient les conséquences ?
english: Supposing the project fails, what would the consequences be?
tip: 'Même si' + indicative (not subjunctive): 'même si tu viens' = even if you come.

target: Ces tableaux ont été peints par un artiste local.
english: These paintings were painted by a local artist.
tip: Passive: être + past participle. 'Peints' agrees with 'tableaux' (masculine plural).

target: Certes, c'est difficile, mais pas impossible.
english: Certainly, it's difficult, but not impossible.
tip: Certes...mais: 'admittedly...but', concessive structure.

target: Je me suis fait voler mon téléphone.
english: I had my phone stolen.
tip: Se faire + infinitive can express involuntary events (something done to you).

target: Il m'a été impossible de la joindre.
english: It was impossible for me to reach her.
tip: Il m'a été + adjective + de: impersonal with indirect object.

target: D'ailleurs, je voulais te poser une question.
english: By the way, I wanted to ask you a question.
tip: D'ailleurs: 'moreover/by the way', adds related information.

target: Il vaut mieux éviter ce quartier la nuit.
english: It's better to avoid this neighbourhood at night.
tip: Il vaut mieux + infinitive: impersonal 'it's better to'.

target: Tandis que les uns travaillent, les autres se reposent.
english: While some work, others rest.
tip: Tandis que: 'while/whereas', can show contrast or simultaneity.

target: Il est temps de passer à l'action.
english: It is time to take action.
tip: 'Être à' for location: 'ils sont à l'aéroport' = they are at the airport.

target: Le pont sera inauguré le mois prochain.
english: The bridge will be inaugurated next month.
tip: Future passive: 'sera inauguré' (will be inaugurated). Être in future + past participle.
